result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A keeps every entry on one line and scrolls horizontally. Its WARN/ERROR rows get a background band, a left-edge marker and bold text, and the level words line up in a column. B looks similar but wraps the long WARN/ERROR lines into ragged continuation lines, which breaks the one-entry-per-line scanning the request needs. B is still easy to read because it uses slightly looser spacing and shows the full timestamps. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B keeps each entry on a single line and scrolls horizontally, so the columns stay intact. A wraps the long WARN and ERROR entries onto ragged continuation lines, which is the exact failure rubric item 2 describes. Both use a comfortable monospace face, aligned level columns, background bands with a left marker for problems, and appear self-contained; B's lines are slightly tighter and it drops the date from the timestamp, but neither hurts scanning.
